The area of each rectangle is $6$, so the area of the square must be divisible by $6$. The
smallest square side length that satisfies this is $6$. It is easy to see that we can tile
a $6$ by $6$ square with $2$ by $3$ rectangles - split the rows into pairs of two, then
cover each pair with two rectangles laid end-to-end. Since the area of the square is
$6^2=36$, and each rectangle has area $6$, the number of rectangles required is
$\boxed{6}$.
